info.name: Rentra API v1
info.description:
Rentra rental-management REST API (SRS 9.3), the interface the Flutter clients consume.

## Getting started

1. Pick the **Rentra - Local** environment (or set `base_url` on the collection).
2. Run **Auth > Login (owner)** or **Auth > Login (renter)**. The response token is saved automatically into `owner_token` / `renter_token`, and into `token`, which every other request uses.
3. Switch roles at any time with **Auth > Use owner token** / **Use renter token**.

Every request except the public feed and the auth endpoints sends `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` through collection-level auth.

## Roles

There are two: **owner** and **renter**. A renter browses listings, applies, and becomes the tenant once an owner accepts; the same account then submits the monthly rent and bills. Endpoints are scoped by role and by ownership (BR-010), so a request for someone else's record answers 403, never someone else's data.

## Conventions

- All responses are JSON. Send `Accept: application/json`, which this collection does for you.
- Validation failures answer `422` with `{ "message", "errors": { field: ["..."] } }`.
- Authorisation failures answer `403`; a missing or revoked token answers `401`.
- Lists are paginated: `data`, `links`, `meta.current_page`, `meta.per_page`, `meta.total`. Most accept `per_page` (1-50).
- Money is a decimal **string** with two places (`"50000.00"`), never a float.
- `PATCH /tenancies/{id}` and `PATCH /properties/{id}` **replace** the record rather than merging: send the whole payload, not just the changed field.
- File uploads are `multipart/form-data`; everything else is JSON.

item.name: Listings (public)
item.description: SRS 5.5 / FR-APP-001 to FR-APP-004. Open to guests - no token needed. Only published **and** available listings appear (BR-001); a house let floor by floor stays out of the feed and its floors appear instead (BR-013).

request.description:
The public feed, rate limited to 120 requests a minute. Saves the first result's id into `{{property_id}}` for the requests below.

The address and full contact details are withheld from guests; sign in to see them (`contact_requires_login` says which you are getting).
Full detail with gallery and videos. A draft, inactive, or occupied listing answers `404` - its existence is not disclosed (SRS 12).

item.name: Applications
item.description: SRS FR-APP-005/006. A renter applies for a published listing; the owner of that listing responds. Withdrawal belongs to the renter and is done on the web.

request.description:
Role-aware (BR-010): a **renter** sees the applications they sent, an **owner** sees the ones sent about their own listings. Nobody sees anything else.

The owner's rows carry the `renter` object so you know who is asking.

exec: pm.test('201, or 422 if an inquiry is already open', function () {

request.description:
Renter only. `message` is required, 10-2000 characters. `contact_phone` is optional and defaults to the profile number.

A **second open inquiry** for the same property answers `422` rather than creating a duplicate the owner has to reconcile. An owner applying, or applying to an unpublished listing, answers `403`. Rate limited to 10 a minute.

Owner of the listed property only. `status` is one of `pending`, `reviewed`, `accepted`, `rejected` - **not** `withdrawn`, which only the renter can set.

`owner_note` is shown to the renter. Accepting does not create the tenancy; do that with **Tenancies > Assign a renter**.

item.name: Properties (owner)
item.description: SRS FR-PROP-001 to FR-PROP-005. Owner only - the whole group answers `403` for a renter, before any policy runs.

request.description: Your own portfolio, newest first. Houses let floor by floor appear once, with their floors nested under them (BR-013).

formdata.value: Bright upper portion with a separate entrance.

formdata.description: REQUIRED: at least 3 photos (jpeg/jpg/png/webp, 4 MB each)

request.description:
**multipart/form-data**, because of the photos.

FR-PROP-003: a listing needs **at least 3 photos** and holds at most 12. Attach files to the `images[]` rows before sending - Postman shows a file picker there.

Set `rental_mode` to `by_floor` to make this a container house: it then carries no rent of its own and never reaches the feed; you add and publish each floor separately (BR-013).
Your own property with gallery, videos, and floors. Another owner's property answers `403`; an archived one answers `404` (BR-009).

formdata.description: Only needed while the listing is short of 3 photos

request.description:
**This replaces the listing rather than patching it.** `type`, `title`, `area`, `address`, `rent_amount`, `status` and `publication_status` are required on every call; sending one field answers `422`.

The photo minimum counts what the listing **already holds**, so a text-only edit does not make you re-upload the gallery. You only attach `images[]` while the listing is still short of 3.

Setting `publication_status` to `published` while `status` is `available` is what puts it in the public feed (BR-001).

item.name: Tenancies
item.description: SRS FR-TEN-001 to FR-TEN-005. Reading is role-aware; every write is owner only.

request.description: An **owner** sees the tenancies on their properties; a **renter** sees their own, current and past (BR-010). A renter may hold more than one.

exec: console.log('Temporary password (shown once, never stored): ' + body.temporary_password);

request.description:
FR-TEN-001. Two ways to name the renter:

- `"renter_mode": "existing"` with `renter_id` - link an account that already exists.
- `"renter_mode": "new"` with `renter_name` and `renter_email` and/or `renter_phone` - the account is created for them, and a **temporary password is returned once** in `temporary_password` (NFR-SEC-008: never stored, never logged, so capture it now).

A property already under an active tenancy answers `403` (BR-002). Assigning marks the property occupied, which takes it out of the public feed.
Readable by the owner of the property and by the renter on it. Anyone else answers `403`.

body.raw:
{
  "start_date": "2026-09-01",
  "end_date": null,
  "agreed_rent": "58000.00",
  "deposit": "110000.00",
  "billing_day": 7,
  "notes": "Rent revised at the annual review."
}

request.description:
FR-TEN-002. **This replaces the terms rather than patching them**: `start_date` and `agreed_rent` are required on every call, so send the whole block.

The property and the renter are deliberately not editable - changing them would rewrite tenancy history (FR-TEN-004). A renter calling this answers `403`.

FR-TEN-005. Frees the property and keeps the whole history - the tenancy and its monthly records stay readable.

`property_status` is where the property lands: `available` or `inactive`. It may **not** be `occupied`, since the tenancy is over.

item.name: Monthly records
item.description:
Monthly submissions separate owner receivables from bills paid directly to providers. Review approval verifies and freezes a submission; it does not mean paid. Payment status and immutable partial-payment history are separate.

**The order matters:** create -> attach a receipt for every charge -> submit. Submitting with an unevidenced charge answers `422`, and once submitted the renter can change nothing until the owner approves or returns it (BR-004).

request.description:
Scoped by role before any filter is applied (BR-010): an owner sees the submissions across their portfolio - this is the approval queue - and a renter sees their own months.

Each row carries `proofs_count`, so a client can flag a thin submission before opening it.

exec: console.log('monthly_record_id set - now attach a receipt for every charge.');
pm.test('201, or 422 if this month already exists', function () {

body.raw:
{
  "tenancy_id": {{tenancy_id}},
  "period_month": "2026-08",

  "rent_amount": "55000.00",
  "electricity_amount": "4200.50",
  "gas_amount": "1100.00",
  "water_amount": "0.00",
  "internet_amount": "3500.00",
  "maintenance_amount": "0.00",
  "other_amount": "0.00",

  "notes": "Internet bill was higher this month because of the upgrade."
}

request.description:
Renter only, and only on **their own active tenancy**.

`period_month` is `YYYY-MM` and is normalised to the first of the month. One record per tenancy per month (BR-003) - a repeat answers `422`.

Every amount is optional and defaults to zero. `total_amount` is derived by the server (BR-012); do not send it. The record starts as a **draft**.

formdata.description: rent | electricity | gas | water | internet | maintenance | other
jpeg/jpg/png/webp/pdf, up to 8 MB, at most 5 per category

request.description:
**multipart/form-data.** FR-MON-003. Repeat this once per charged category - a photo of the bill or the payment receipt.

Proofs are stored on a **private** disk (NFR-SEC-007). They are never a public URL: the response hands back a `download_url` that runs the policy first, so only the renter who uploaded it and the owner of that property can open it.

Works only while the record is a draft or has been returned. A submitted or frozen record answers `403` (BR-004).

exec: pm.test('200, or 422 while a charge has no receipt', function () {

request.description:
FR-MON-005. Moves the record to **pending** and notifies the owner.

Two things stop it:
- an empty record (nothing charged) answers `422` on `rent_amount`;
- **any charge without a receipt** answers `422` on `files`, naming the categories - the owner must be able to verify what they are approving.

After this the renter can change nothing: no amounts, no new receipts, no deletions (BR-004).
Both parties see the same thing: every amount, and the proofs grouped by category with an authorised `download_url` each.

Only while the record is a **draft** or has been **returned** by the owner. A pending or frozen record answers `403` (BR-004 / BR-006).

Any category left out is written back as zero, so send the full set. The total is recalculated server side.
Owner only. Appends to immutable payment history and recalculates total received, rent received, outstanding receivable, and payment status. It does not change review approval status.

FR-MON-006/008. The owner accepts the submitted record and evidence. The record becomes **approved and frozen**: neither side edits it again without a reopen. Approval is a review state and does not change `payment_status`.

FR-MON-007. Hands the month back to the renter with a reason they will see (5-1000 characters), and makes it editable again so they can fix it and resubmit.

This is the way out of a submission that is missing or unclear - the lock is about the review window, not a one-way door.
FR-MON-009. Unfreezes an approved record and returns it to pending. Needs a reason and is written to the audit log, because it undoes a decision that was already final.

item.name: Maintenance
item.description: SRS FR-MNT-001 to FR-MNT-004. The renter raises an issue; both parties share one timeline; only the owner moves the status.

request.description: Role-aware: an owner sees the issues raised against their properties, a renter sees their own.

formdata.value: The cold tap drips constantly and the cupboard below is getting damp.

formdata.description: Optional, up to 6 photos or PDFs

request.description:
**multipart/form-data**, because issue photos can be attached.

FR-MNT-001/002. Attachments can show the inside of a home, so they live on the private disk and are served through an authorised download route like the proofs. The request opens as **pending**.

Carries the attachments and the full `timeline` of status changes and comments.

`allowed_transitions` lists exactly which statuses this request may move to next, so a client can render only the legal buttons (SRS 12).

FR-MNT-004. Both the owner and the renter write to the same timeline. A comment is **not** a status change - the request stays where it is.

Anyone not party to the tenancy answers `403`.

FR-MNT-003. Owner only - a renter answers `403`.

Transitions are enforced: `pending` -> `in_progress`, `completed` or `cancelled`; `in_progress` -> `completed` or `cancelled`; a completed or cancelled request moves nowhere. An illegal jump answers `422`. The optional `comment` is added to the timeline alongside the change.

item.name: Conversations
item.description: Tenantism messaging API. Conversations are created from accepted/reviewed applications and are visible only to the owner and renter on that application.

request.description: Role-aware inbox for the signed-in user. Includes the related property, application, participants, latest message, and `unread_messages_count` for badge UI.
Returns the conversation with its message thread. Messages from the other participant are marked as read when this endpoint is opened.

exec: pm.test('201 or 200 with message data', function () {

request.description: Sends a message as the signed-in participant. `body` is required and may be up to 5000 characters. Pending or rejected applications do not allow messaging.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: SRS FR-NOT-001/003. In-app notifications for both roles.

request.description:
Newest first, for the account behind the token. `meta.unread_count` drives the badge.

Types you will see: `application.submitted`, `application.status_changed`, `monthly_record.submitted`, `monthly_record.approved`, `monthly_record.rejected`, `tenancy.assigned`, and the maintenance ones. Each carries an `action_url` to open.

An **empty or omitted** `ids` marks everything read. Pass specific ids to mark just those.

Each id is authorised on its own, so a stray id belonging to another account answers `403` rather than being quietly skipped.

Returns the new `unread_count`.
